lessons.title: DID, toll-free, shared cost, UIFN
lessons.why: The number type is a cost and a failure-domain choice.
paras: Connect sells four types, in more than 100 countries, billed per day plus per-minute telephony. A US DID in the Oregon worked example is 0.030 USD per day, 0.0022 USD per inbound minute, and outbound US telephony at 0.0048 USD per minute.

US toll-free numbers are registered with SOMOS. AWS can place them on more than one carrier, which is why they cost more and why they are the more resilient public number. The appendix example charges 0 USD per day for the first 12 months of the free tier and 0.06 USD per day after. Country rates that are not in that example must be read from the global telephony table, not invented.
points: DID is one carrier. It presents a local number. It is not load-balanced across carriers.
You can mix DID and toll-free on one instance.
Inbound telephony in the example is charged per minute with a 60 second minimum.
Voice service is a second charge, 0.038 or 0.018 USD per minute depending on the product form, billed per second with a 10 second minimum.
lessons.mistake: Quoting a toll-free per-minute rate you did not look up.

lessons.title: Claiming and the false 'limit' on the first number
lessons.why: The first claim is a Support conversation more often than people expect.
paras: The default quota is 10 numbers per instance, and it is adjustable. The docs also say you can see 'You've reached the limit of Phone Numbers' the first time you claim, and that those failures need Support.

Concurrent campaign calls default to 0. Outbound calling destinations are allowed by country. A new instance that cannot dial the country you care about is a quota or a country allow list, not a flow bug.
points: Raise the call concurrency quota before you publish the number.
Associate the number with a flow or the caller hears nothing useful.
For Global Resiliency, numbers join a traffic distribution group.
Write down the carrier and the country. Porting later depends on both.
lessons.mistake: Retrying the claim button until it works.

number.n: Per instance, and the first claim can still fail

lessons.title: Porting without losing the rollback
lessons.why: A port is a date with the losing carrier. It is not a flow change.
paras: You submit the port with the same kind of Support request the quota page describes. You need a letter of authorization and a firm order commit date. Until that date, the old platform still owns the number.
Dual-run means the old platform and Connect are both built, and you can move the number back if the first day fails. Practice the rollback before the port window, not during it.
points: Match the caller ID and any CNAM story you actually have. Do not promise caller-name display the product does not set.
Internal extensions can stay on CUCM. Only the public number has to move.
Update the CRM screen pop to the new ContactId in the same window.
Tell the WFM and recording tools the storage path before the port, or the first day has no recordings in the old tool.
lessons.mistake: Porting on Friday because the flow 'looks done'.

lessons.title: SIP, external voice, and what is not a trunk in the CUCM sense
lessons.why: Connect does not give you a CUCM SIP trunk page. It gives you native telephony, transfers to numbers, and an external voice connector for analytics.
paras: Transfer to phone number is how a flow or an agent sends a call to a CUCM route point, a Webex Calling number, or a mobile. The call leaves Connect and the other system owns the media from there.

The pricing appendix describes an external voice connector at 0.032 USD per minute and 100 USD per connector per day, for analytics on voice that stays on another system. The default quota for external voice analytics connectors is 0 until you request them. That is a different product from claiming a DID.
points: Do not design a SIP trunk in CUCM and assume Connect will register to it as a phone.
One-way audio after a transfer is often the other system's codec or network, not the CCP.
External voice is for analytics on audio you already have.
Campaign answering-machine detection is Check call progress, and only in campaign flows.
lessons.mistake: Drawing a SIP trunk icon between CUCM and Connect and assigning a dial-peer as if both were CUCM.

lessons.title: Outbound calls and caller ID
lessons.why: Outbound is a queue setting, a permission, and a country quota.
paras: The queue's outbound caller ID is the number the customer sees. It must be a number you are allowed to present. The origination number on a 911 call is the same idea: responders can call back only if that number accepts inbound calls.
High-volume outbound became outbound campaigns on 20 June 2022. Campaign voice on Connect Customer is 0.045 USD per minute instead of 0.038.
points: StartOutboundVoiceContact is an API. Guard it.
An outbound whisper flow runs before the customer and agent join. Recording for outbound is set there.
Call phone number is the block that dials from an outbound whisper flow.
Country allow lists block destinations even when the flow is correct.
lessons.mistake: Using a personal mobile as the outbound caller ID.
